title: Appeals Desk Note: Denied PAP Therapy Equipment Rental Months
content:
# Appealing a Denied PAP Therapy Equipment Rental Month

**Rule.** A denied PAP Therapy Equipment rental month may be appealed through a redetermination appeal request naming that denied line as the related bill. The appeal is filed no later than the coverage class's redetermination window in days after the denial is received, counting calendar days from the day after the denied line's adjudication date with the boundary day included. The length of that window is the coverage class's redetermination window, a value of Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility.

**Denials that are not appealed.** A denial for "cap reached", "same or similar" or "inpatient stay" is not appealed, because the facts behind it are correct. A denial for "compliance not documented" or "re-evaluation missing" is appealed only when the missing proof was in fact on file before the denial.

**One at a time.** One appeal per denied line is open at a time.

**Evidence.** The adjudication date is read from the denied line in the device's billing history; the appeal names that same line.

## Denial reasons

| Denial reason | Appealed |
|---|---|
| cap reached | no |
| same or similar | no |
| inpatient stay | no |
| compliance not documented | only when the missing proof was on file before the denial |
| re-evaluation missing | only when the missing proof was on file before the denial |

## The filing window, element by element

- The clock starts when the denial is received, as the denied line's adjudication date shows.
- Day 1 is the day after the adjudication date; days are calendar days.
- The last day of the window is included: an appeal filed on it is in time, one filed the day after is not.

**Worked window (hypothetical coverage class with a 120-day window).** A line adjudicated on 1 March: day 1 is 2 March and day 120 is 29 June. An appeal filed on 29 June is in time; one filed on 30 June is late.
